doc: Media shapes several SDKs share, tried after every dialect's own cases: a part that names its bytes' MIME type beside them, a bare stored reference, and a part whose kind member nests the location under its own name. These were the Rust media fallback; what stays in Rust is the generic decoding - a data URL's header, a stored reference's media type, bytes against a location - which is about values, not producers.

content_blocks.doc: A part declaring its MIME type beside its bytes, with no `type` member required - LangChain Python and several SDKs write attachments this way. The kind comes from the media type; the value decides whether it is bytes, a location or a stored reference, whose own media type then wins.

A bare stored reference: ingestion replaces inline bytes with SideSeat's own reference, which carries the media type the bytes were stored under, so a part holding one and nothing a dialect recognised is that file. AutoGen's Image serialises to exactly this.

A part whose `type` nests its location under its own name - OpenInference's dotted families unflatten to this - with the location one or two levels down, as a URL or as bytes. The kind is the stated one; the value says whether it is a data URL, a reference, a location or bytes.
